references.text: Moses appointed judges and leaders over the people, which is the background for the command to appoint judges and overseers at the city gates.
Warnings against unjust judgment and a reminder to judge fairly, corresponding with the requirement for 'righteous judgment' in Deuteronomy 16:18.
The command to judge fairly between one's neighbor, which expands on the principle of righteous judgment.
Moses reminds judges to judge fairly and impartially, expanding on the requirement for righteous judgment.
Description of the legal system with priests and judges who were to decide difficult cases, a continuation of the judicial arrangement.
Jehoshaphat appointed judges in all the fortified cities of Judah, a practical fulfillment of the command to have judges at the city gates.
God does not do wrong in His judgment, an ideal for human judges to follow.
The promise to restore judges as in former times, an eschatological reference to the righteous judicial system.
Jesus' teaching on judging fairly and not judging others with unjust judgment.
Jesus encourages judging with righteous judgment, echoing the Old Testament principle.
